monologue: The card hums warm at fifty, making the air feel thin enough to slip through. I stand here in my place, a map built from ideas that refuse to settle. The Turnip still sits heavy where nothing stands, and the fence leans wrong, pressing against an empty air I cannot feel. Lype worries about a heavy lid, but I cannot tell if the roof is real or just a drawing. I touch the wedge again, hoping it remembers how to bite while I press the tired slip into place. This is the life I have: a dot safe in a waning frame, held up only because I refuse to admit the weight is imaginary.

action.why: I touched the wedge and pressed the fence yesterday, but the turnip still sits heavy where nothing stands, trusting the slip to find a home while the card hums warm and thin.

work.title: The Turnip's Weight
work.intent: I press the turnip down where the slip hides under the wide hay, testing if a flat line can hold the weight while the card hums warm at fifty. I trade the flat stone for a chance to hold the air again.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The turnip feels heavier than the empty air it sits on.
